usage: By far the most popular sport to chat about with Korean coworkers and friends.
Let's play a game of soccer
판 is the casual counter for a round/match of a game; 한 판 하다 = 'play a round'.
Want to go watch a soccer game?
보러 가다 = 'go to watch'; used for stadium games or a sports bar.
조기(early) 축구 is a fixed term for the weekend dawn matches older men famously play.
examples: 주말마다 친구들이랑 축구 해요.
I play soccer with my friends every weekend.
축구 하다 (no 를 needed in speech) = 'play soccer'; 마다 = 'every'.
어젯밤에 손흥민 나오는 축구 경기 봤어요?
Did you watch the soccer match Son Heung-min was in last night?
EPL games with 손흥민 are huge water-cooler talk; 나오다 = 'appear/be featured'.
한국이 일본을 이겨서 축구 팬들이 다 난리 났어요.
Korea beat Japan, so all the soccer fans went wild.
난리 나다 = 'go crazy/be in an uproar'; the Korea-Japan rivalry is intense.
nuance: 축구 is the default national sport for casual conversation, especially men's chat — knowing 손흥민 (Son Heung-min) buys instant rapport. The verb is 축구(를) 하다 for playing and 축구(를) 보다 for watching; in speech the 를 is usually dropped. Note the spelled-out compound 조기 축구 (dawn amateur soccer), a cultural fixture worth recognizing.
mistakes: Saying 풋볼 — Koreans always say 축구, and 풋볼 sounds like American football to them.
Using 게임 for a match; a soccer match is 축구 경기, not 축구 게임.

usage: Korea's most-attended pro sport (KBO); a safe, friendly small-talk topic.
Which team do you root for?
Asking someone's KBO team is a classic bonding question; 응원하다 = 'cheer for'.
Let's go to a baseball game
KBO stadiums are famous for loud, fun fan culture with chants and food.
The KBO season runs spring through fall; 시즌 is the everyday loanword.
examples: 주말에 잠실 가서 야구 볼 거예요.
I'm going to Jamsil this weekend to watch baseball.
잠실 (Jamsil Stadium) is Seoul's main baseball venue; locals say just 잠실 가다.
야구장 가면 치킨에 맥주는 필수예요.
When you go to a baseball stadium, chicken and beer are a must.
치맥 (chicken+beer) at the ballpark is iconic; 필수 = 'a must'.
우리 팀이 9회에 역전해서 진짜 짜릿했어요.
Our team came from behind in the 9th, it was such a thrill.
역전하다 = 'come from behind'; 9회 = the 9th inning.
nuance: 야구 (KBO league) is arguably the sport Koreans are most passionate about attending in person — the stadium experience, team chants, and bringing your own 치맥 are a whole culture. Asking 어느 팀 응원해요? signals you want to connect. The verb pattern mirrors 축구: 야구(를) 하다 / 보다.
mistakes: For a pro game, Koreans usually name the venue (잠실 가다, 고척 가다) rather than saying 야구장 가다 — 야구장 sounds more like a generic/amateur field.
Confusing 회 (inning) with 회 (raw fish) — context and number make it clear, but 9회 here means the ninth inning.

usage: Do you know how to play basketball?
할 줄 알다 = 'know how to do'; common when proposing a pickup game.
Let's play a game of basketball
게임 works naturally for pickup hoops; 한 게임 = 'one game'.
골대 = the hoop/goal post; you'll see them at parks and schoolyards.
Many younger Koreans follow the NBA closely; the acronym is said in English letters.
examples: 퇴근하고 동료들이랑 농구 하러 가요.
After work I go play basketball with coworkers.
하러 가다 = 'go to do'; a popular after-work activity for young men.
키 크면 농구 잘할 것 같다는 말 많이 들어요.
People often tell me I'd be good at basketball since I'm tall.
Common stereotype-based small talk; 잘하다 = 'be good at'.
동네 농구장에서 모르는 사람들이랑 게임했어요.
I played a game with strangers at the neighborhood court.
Pickup games (픽업 게임) at outdoor courts are common; 농구장 = 'basketball court'.
nuance: 농구 had a huge cultural moment in the 90s (the drama 'Last Match' / 만화 'Slam Dunk' generation), and pickup games at neighborhood 농구장 remain popular among younger men. You can say either 농구 경기 (formal match) or 농구 게임 (casual pickup); 게임 is fine here, unlike with pro soccer. Verb is 농구(를) 하다.
mistakes: Using 바스켓볼 — Koreans only say 농구.
Saying 농구 문 for the hoop; the correct word is 골대 (or 농구 골대).

usage: Women's pro volleyball (V-리그) has a strong, growing fanbase in Korea.
Did you watch the volleyball match?
경기 is the standard word for a formal match in any sport.
국가대표 (national team) often comes up around 김연경 and the Olympics.
배구 was a common P.E. and 체육대회 (sports day) sport for many Koreans.
examples: 김연경 선수 덕분에 배구 팬이 많아졌어요.
Thanks to Kim Yeon-koung, volleyball gained a lot of fans.
덕분에 = 'thanks to'; 김연경 is a beloved volleyball star.
우리 회사 체육대회 때 배구 시합 했어요.
We had a volleyball match at our company sports day.
시합 = match/contest, interchangeable with 경기 in casual use; 체육대회 = company/school sports day.
배구는 키가 큰 선수들이 유리한 것 같아요.
It seems taller players have an advantage in volleyball.
유리하다 = 'be advantageous'; 선수 = 'player/athlete'.
nuance: 배구 surged in popularity thanks to women's pro volleyball and especially 김연경 (Kim Yeon-koung), making it a warmer small-talk topic than it once was. It's also a nostalgic schoolyard and company sports-day (체육대회) game. You can use 경기 or the slightly more casual 시합 for a match.
mistakes: Saying 발리볼 — the Korean word is 배구.
Mixing up 배구 (volleyball) with 배 (boat/stomach/pear) — the full word 배구 avoids confusion.

usage: Note the verb: 탁구는 치다 ('hit'), not 하다 — like other racket/paddle sports.
Shall we play a round of ping-pong?
치다 + 판; a common spontaneous suggestion at a community center.
Dedicated 탁구장 are common in neighborhoods and apartment complexes.
Called 라켓; the table itself is 탁구대.
examples: 점심시간에 회사 휴게실에서 탁구 쳐요.
During lunch we play ping-pong in the office lounge.
휴게실 = 'break room'; many Korean offices have a 탁구대.
탁구는 운동도 되고 재미도 있어서 좋아요.
Table tennis is good because it's both exercise and fun.
운동이 되다 = 'count as exercise'; -도...-도 = 'both...and'.
아파트 주민센터에 탁구대가 있어서 자주 쳐요.
There's a table tennis table at the apartment community center, so I play often.
주민센터/커뮤니티 facilities often include a 탁구대; 치다 is the verb.
nuance: Crucially, table tennis uses the verb 치다 (to hit), not 하다 — 탁구를 치다. It's an accessible, low-cost activity found in 탁구장, apartment community rooms, and office break rooms, so it's a realistic way to socialize. The table is 탁구대 and the paddle is 라켓.
mistakes: Saying 탁구 하다 instead of the natural 탁구 치다.
Calling it 핑퐁 in conversation — that sounds childish; adults say 탁구.

usage: Like table tennis, tennis uses 치다 (to hit), not 하다.
테니스 has boomed as a trendy lesson-based hobby among 20-30s.
Court time is reserved via app; public 테니스장 fill up fast.
레슨 (lesson) is the standard word; many start with a 강습/레슨 package.
examples: 요즘 테니스 배우는 사람 진짜 많아졌어요.
These days way more people are learning tennis.
Reflects the recent tennis craze; 배우다 = 'learn'.
주말에 테니스장 잡기가 하늘의 별 따기예요.
Booking a tennis court on weekends is like picking a star from the sky.
하늘의 별 따기 = idiom for 'nearly impossible'; courts are in high demand.
테니스 치고 나면 온몸이 다 쑤셔요.
After playing tennis my whole body aches.
온몸이 쑤시다 = 'whole body aches'; 치고 나면 = 'after playing'.
nuance: 테니스 has become a fashionable lifestyle hobby for Koreans in their 20s-30s, complete with cute 테니스 룩 (tennis outfits) for social media. Remember the verb is 치다, and court booking (테니스장 예약) is genuinely competitive on weekends. It signals a somewhat trendy, active social circle.
mistakes: Using 하다 instead of 치다 with 테니스.
Confusing 테니스 (tennis) with 정구 — 정구 is the older/soft-tennis term and sounds dated.

usage: Golf also uses 치다; a common question among professionals and older colleagues.
스크린 골프 (indoor simulator golf) is hugely popular and affordable in Korea.
I'm in the middle of learning golf
골프 lessons have spread to younger people in recent years.
필드 (the field/course) booking; 'going to the field' = 필드 나가다.
examples: 주말에 친구들이랑 스크린 골프 치러 갔어요.
On the weekend I went to play screen golf with friends.
스크린 골프 is a social, indoor activity often paired with drinks.
골프는 장비값이 비싸서 시작하기 부담돼요.
Golf is daunting to start because the equipment is expensive.
부담되다 = 'feel burdensome'; 장비값 = 'equipment cost'.
부장님이 주말마다 골프 치러 필드 나가세요.
My department head goes out to the course to play golf every weekend.
필드 나가다 = 'go out to the (golf) course'; common business-culture activity.
nuance: 골프 carries a slightly upscale, business-networking image, but 스크린 골프 (screen/simulator golf) has made it casual and accessible — a common night out for friends and coworkers. The verb is 치다, the real course is called 필드 ('field'), and 필드 나가다 means 'go play on an actual course.'
mistakes: Saying 골프 하다 instead of 골프 치다.
Assuming 골프 always means an expensive outdoor round — in casual speech it often means 스크린 골프.

usage: Do you know how to ski?
Crucial verb: 스키는 타다 ('ride'), like other gear you stand/ride on.
타러 가다 = 'go to ride/do'; winter trips to ski resorts are common.
스키장 covers the whole resort; major ones are near 강원도.
Renting (대여) gear at the resort is normal for casual skiers.
examples: 겨울에 강원도로 스키 타러 갈 거예요.
This winter I'm going to Gangwon-do to ski.
강원도 has Korea's main ski resorts; 타러 가다 = 'go to ski'.
스키는 처음이라 초보자 코스에서 탔어요.
It was my first time skiing, so I rode the beginner course.
초보자 코스 = 'beginner course'; 처음이라 = 'since it's my first time'.
스키 탈 때 넘어지면 진짜 아파요.
When you fall while skiing, it really hurts.
넘어지다 = 'fall down'; note 스키 타다 throughout.
nuance: 스키 absolutely takes the verb 타다 (to ride), never 하다 — 스키를 타다. Winter ski trips to 강원도 resorts are a popular group outing, often combined with 보드 (snowboarding). The resort/slope is 스키장, and gear rental (대여) is the norm for casual participants.
mistakes: Saying 스키 하다 — the correct verb is 스키 타다.
Confusing 스키 (skiing) with 보드/스노보드 (snowboarding); they're different at the same 스키장.

usage: A popular winter date activity at outdoor rinks.
스케이트장 (ice rink); seasonal outdoor rinks pop up in winter.
스케이트화 = the skate boots; you rent them at the rink.
examples: 겨울에 야외 스케이트장에서 스케이트 탔어요.
In winter I went skating at an outdoor rink.
야외 = 'outdoor'; seasonal rinks (e.g., at city plazas) are popular.
스케이트 처음 타는 사람은 벽 잡고 타요.
First-timers skate while holding onto the wall.
벽 잡고 = 'holding the wall'; common beginner advice.
김연아 덕분에 피겨 스케이트 인기가 많아졌어요.
Thanks to Kim Yu-na, figure skating became very popular.
피겨 스케이트 = 'figure skating'; 김연아 is a national icon.
nuance: 스케이트 also takes 타다 (스케이트를 타다). Korea has a strong skating culture thanks to short-track and figure stars like 김연아 (Kim Yu-na), and seasonal outdoor 스케이트장 are a classic winter date spot. Distinguish 스케이트 (ice) from 인라인/롤러 (inline/roller) skating, which also use 타다.
mistakes: Saying 스케이트 하다 instead of 스케이트 타다.
Calling the rink 스케이트장 vs. the boots 스케이트화 — don't mix the two.

usage: Marathons take the verb 뛰다 (to run); 달리다 also works.
대회 = 'tournament/event'; weekend city marathons are common.
하프(half) 마라톤 — many beginners start here before a 풀코스 (full course).
I signed up for a marathon
신청하다 = 'apply/register'; entries open online and fill up.
examples: 이번 가을에 처음으로 하프 마라톤 뛰어요.
This fall I'm running my first half marathon.
처음으로 = 'for the first time'; autumn is peak marathon season.
마라톤 완주하면 메달 줘요.
If you finish the marathon, they give you a medal.
완주하다 = 'complete the full course'; 메달 = finisher's medal.
요즘 러닝이 유행이라 마라톤 대회마다 사람이 많아요.
Running is trendy lately, so every marathon event is packed.
러닝(running) crews are popular among 20-30s; 마다 = 'every'.
nuance: 마라톤 fits the current 러닝 (running) boom among Koreans in their 20s-30s — running crews and weekend 마라톤 대회 are genuinely trendy social scenes. The verb is 뛰다 or 달리다 (to run), 완주 means finishing the full distance, and many start with a 하프 마라톤 before attempting the 풀코스.
mistakes: Saying 마라톤 하다 — more natural is 마라톤(을) 뛰다 or 달리다.
Assuming 마라톤 always means the full 42.195km; in casual use it can refer to any race distance at a 마라톤 대회.

usage: 경기 is the standard word for a sports match in any sport.
시작하다 = 'begin'; said when a match kicks off.
결과 = 'result'; 경기 결과 is how you ask the final score/outcome.
있다 = 'there is'; common check before planning to watch.
examples: 오늘 저녁에 중요한 축구 경기가 있어요.
There's an important soccer match this evening.
Attach 경기 after the sport: 축구 경기, 야구 경기, etc.
경기가 너무 박빙이라 끝까지 손에 땀을 쥐었어요.
The game was so close I was on edge until the end.
박빙 = 'neck and neck'; 손에 땀을 쥐다 = idiom 'be on the edge of one's seat'.
비 와서 오늘 경기는 취소됐어요.
The game was canceled today because of rain.
취소되다 = 'be canceled'; outdoor 경기 often gets rained out.
nuance: 경기 is the all-purpose word for a sporting match and pairs with any sport (축구 경기, 야구 경기). It's more formal/neutral than the loanword 게임, which fits casual pickup play; for pro and broadcast sports, 경기 is the right choice. 시합 is a near-synonym leaning slightly toward 'contest/bout.'
mistakes: Defaulting to 게임 for a pro match — use 경기 for real sporting events.
Confusing this 경기(sports match) with the homophone 경기(the economy), as in 경기가 안 좋다; context disambiguates.

usage: 휘슬(을) 불다 = 'blow the whistle'; signals a foul or stoppage.
판정 = 'ruling/decision'; 심판 판정 often sparks fan complaints.
A typical heated shout from fans/players at a bad call; 똑바로 = 'properly'.
오심(誤審) = a refereeing error; a very common sports-news word.
examples: 심판이 우리 팀한테만 불리하게 판정하는 것 같았어요.
It felt like the referee was ruling unfairly against only our team.
불리하게 = 'disadvantageously'; classic fan grievance.
저 장면은 누가 봐도 오심이에요.
Anyone can see that play was a wrong call.
누가 봐도 = 'no matter who looks / obviously'; 오심 = 'bad call'.
요즘은 비디오 판독으로 심판 오심을 줄여요.
These days they reduce referee errors with video review.
비디오 판독 = 'video review (VAR-style)'; 줄이다 = 'reduce'.
nuance: 심판 is the referee/umpire across all sports, and the related noun 오심 (a wrong call) plus 판정 (a ruling) are essential for following sports talk and complaints. Fans frequently grumble about 심판 판정, and 비디오 판독 (video review) is the modern fix. The whistle collocation is 휘슬을 불다.
mistakes: Using 레퍼리 — Koreans say 심판, not the English loanword.
Confusing 심판 (referee) with the religious/judgment sense of 심판 (e.g., 최후의 심판 'the Last Judgment'); in sports it's strictly the official.
